fruits.extendedStory: The cathedral was begun in 1060, and in 1308 its front was redrawn into the lopsided shape it still has. Inside hangs the Volto Santo, a wooden crucifix that legend says Nicodemus carved. Nearby lies Ilaria del Carretto. Her husband Paolo Guinigi paid Jacopo della Quercia to carve her, and people have looked at her face ever since. The bell tower stands about 60 metres, and 217 steps go up it.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Der Dom wurde 1060 begonnen, und 1308 zeichnete man die Fassade neu, in die schiefe Form, die sie bis heute hat. Drinnen hängt der Volto Santo, ein hölzernes Kruzifix, das der Legende nach Nikodemus schnitzte. Ganz in der Nähe liegt Ilaria del Carretto. Ihr Mann Paolo Guinigi bezahlte Jacopo della Quercia dafür, sie zu hauen, und seither schauen die Leute ihr ins Gesicht. 217 Stufen führen den Glockenturm hinauf, der etwa 60 Meter misst.
localizedExtendedStory.en: The cathedral was begun in 1060, and in 1308 its front was redrawn into the lopsided shape it still has. Inside hangs the Volto Santo, a wooden crucifix that legend says Nicodemus carved. Nearby lies Ilaria del Carretto. Her husband Paolo Guinigi paid Jacopo della Quercia to carve her, and people have looked at her face ever since. The bell tower stands about 60 metres, and 217 steps go up it.

localizedStory.de: Die Fassade dieses Doms ist absichtlich schief. 1308 wurde sie so neu gezeichnet.
localizedStory.en: The front of this cathedral is deliberately lopsided. It was redrawn that way in 1308.

fruits.name: Cattedrale di San Martino
fruits.story: The front of this cathedral is deliberately lopsided. It was redrawn that way in 1308.

fruits.extendedStory: This church stands on the old Roman forum, the hinge the whole city turned on. Its name appears in writing in 795 as ad foro, meaning at the forum. Pope Alexander II wanted the present building, and work began in 1070. Right at the top of the front stands the Archangel Michael in marble, with metal wings, his lance held over a dragon.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Diese Kirche steht auf dem alten römischen Forum, dem Angelpunkt der ganzen Stadt. Zuerst erwähnt wurde sie 795 als ad foro, also am Forum. Papst Alexander II. wollte den heutigen Bau, und 1070 begannen die Arbeiten. Ganz oben auf der Fassade steht der Erzengel Michael aus Marmor, mit Flügeln aus Metall, die Lanze über einem Drachen.
localizedExtendedStory.en: This church stands on the old Roman forum, the hinge the whole city turned on. Its name appears in writing in 795 as ad foro, meaning at the forum. Pope Alexander II wanted the present building, and work began in 1070. Right at the top of the front stands the Archangel Michael in marble, with metal wings, his lance held over a dragon.

localizedStory.de: Hoch oben auf der Fassade steht ein Marmorengel mit Flügeln aus Metall, die Lanze über einem Drachen.
localizedStory.en: High on the front stands a marble angel with metal wings, his lance held over a dragon.

fruits.name: San Michele in Foro
fruits.story: High on the front stands a marble angel with metal wings, his lance held over a dragon.

fruits.extendedStory: Frediano was an Irish bishop who founded a church on this spot in the sixth century. The building you see was begun in 1112. Across its front runs a great mosaic. Part of it was worked by hands trained in the Byzantine manner, part by the Berlinghieri workshop from Lucca itself. Inside rests Santa Zita, who died in 1278. The people of Lucca wanted her here, and here she has stayed.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Frediano war ein irischer Bischof, der hier im sechsten Jahrhundert eine Kirche gründete. Der heutige Bau wurde 1112 begonnen. Über die Fassade zieht sich ein großes Mosaik, teils von byzantinisch geschulten Händen, teils aus der Werkstatt der Berlinghieri aus Lucca selbst. Drinnen ruht Santa Zita, gestorben 1278. Die Lucchesen wollten sie hier haben, und hier ist sie geblieben.
localizedExtendedStory.en: Frediano was an Irish bishop who founded a church on this spot in the sixth century. The building you see was begun in 1112. Across its front runs a great mosaic. Part of it was worked by hands trained in the Byzantine manner, part by the Berlinghieri workshop from Lucca itself. Inside rests Santa Zita, who died in 1278. The people of Lucca wanted her here, and here she has stayed.

localizedStory.de: Ein großes Mosaik bedeckt die ganze Fassade. Gegründet hat die Kirche ein irischer Bischof namens Frediano.
localizedStory.en: A huge mosaic covers the front of this church. An Irish bishop named Frediano founded it.

fruits.name: Basilica di San Frediano
fruits.story: A huge mosaic covers the front of this church. An Irish bishop named Frediano founded it.

fruits.extendedStory: The tower went up in 1301 and carries the name of the Guinigi. Its stonework is Romanesque, the round-arched style of that age. From the street below you look up through 44.25 metres of brick. A family put its name on a tower, and six centuries later that name is still the one people say here.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Der Turm entstand 1301 und trägt den Namen der Guinigi. Das Mauerwerk ist romanisch, der Rundbogenstil jener Zeit. Von der Gasse aus blickt man 44,25 Meter an Backstein hinauf. Eine Familie setzte ihren Namen auf einen Turm, und nach sechs Jahrhunderten ist es immer noch der Name, den man hier nennt.
localizedExtendedStory.en: The tower went up in 1301 and carries the name of the Guinigi. Its stonework is Romanesque, the round-arched style of that age. From the street below you look up through 44.25 metres of brick. A family put its name on a tower, and six centuries later that name is still the one people say here.

localizedStory.de: Die Familie Guinigi gab diesem Turm 1301 ihren Namen. Er ragt 44,25 Meter über die Gasse.
localizedStory.en: The Guinigi family put their name on this tower in 1301. It stands 44.25 metres above the street.

fruits.name: Torre Guinigi
fruits.story: The Guinigi family put their name on this tower in 1301. It stands 44.25 metres above the street.

fruits.extendedStory: The Romans raised an amphitheatre on this spot, outside the walls of their town. It had 55 arches in two tiers and held ten thousand people. When it fell, families built their homes straight onto the ruins and followed the curve. In 1830 the architect Nottolini cleared out the middle, and the oval you stand in is what was left.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Die Römer errichteten hier ein Amphitheater, außerhalb der Mauern ihrer Stadt. Es hatte 55 Bögen in zwei Reihen und fasste zehntausend Menschen. Als es verfiel, bauten Familien ihre Häuser direkt auf die Ruinen und folgten der Rundung. 1830 räumte der Architekt Nottolini die Mitte frei, und das Oval, in dem man steht, blieb übrig.
localizedExtendedStory.en: The Romans raised an amphitheatre on this spot, outside the walls of their town. It had 55 arches in two tiers and held ten thousand people. When it fell, families built their homes straight onto the ruins and followed the curve. In 1830 the architect Nottolini cleared out the middle, and the oval you stand in is what was left.

localizedStory.de: Ein ovaler Platz, der in Wahrheit eine römische Arena ist. Häuser wuchsen auf den Ruinen und bewahrten die Form.
localizedStory.en: An oval square that is really a Roman arena. Houses grew on the ruins and kept its shape.

fruits.name: Piazza Anfiteatro
fruits.story: An oval square that is really a Roman arena. Houses grew on the ruins and kept its shape.

fruits.extendedStory: Giovanni Lazzarini built this gate in 1809, and it faces east towards the road to Florence. Every other gate in the wall carries the name of a saint. This one carries the name of Elisa Baciocchi Bonaparte, Napoleon's sister, princess of Lucca at the time. Naming a gate for someone still alive was a new idea, and it says a good deal about who was in charge.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Giovanni Lazzarini baute dieses Tor 1809, und es blickt nach Osten, zur Straße nach Florenz. Jedes andere Tor der Mauer trägt einen Heiligennamen. Dieses trägt den Namen von Elisa Baciocchi Bonaparte, Napoleons Schwester, damals Fürstin von Lucca. Ein Tor nach einer Lebenden zu benennen war neu, und es verrät einiges darüber, wer hier bestimmte.
localizedExtendedStory.en: Giovanni Lazzarini built this gate in 1809, and it faces east towards the road to Florence. Every other gate in the wall carries the name of a saint. This one carries the name of Elisa Baciocchi Bonaparte, Napoleon's sister, princess of Lucca at the time. Naming a gate for someone still alive was a new idea, and it says a good deal about who was in charge.

localizedStory.de: Luccas Tore tragen Heiligennamen. Dieses von 1809 trägt den Namen einer lebenden Frau.
localizedStory.en: The gates of Lucca are named for saints. This one, opened in 1809, is named for a living woman.

fruits.name: Porta Elisa
fruits.story: The gates of Lucca are named for saints. This one, opened in 1809, is named for a living woman.

fruits.extendedStory: Lucca's wall runs 4 kilometres and 223 metres around the town, with eleven bastions set into it. This is one of them, and an older tower sits swallowed up inside its bulk. Galleries run underneath it. In 2024 they opened as a permanent exhibition about the wall, entered from via delle Conce. In the 1820s Maria Luisa of Bourbon turned the whole circuit into a walking park. That is what people use it for now.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Luccas Mauer läuft 4 Kilometer und 223 Meter um die Stadt, mit elf Bastionen darin. Dies ist eine davon, und in ihrem Leib steckt ein älterer Turm. Darunter ziehen sich Galerien. 2024 öffneten sie als feste Ausstellung über die Mauer, mit Eingang an der via delle Conce. In den 1820er Jahren machte Maria Luisa von Bourbon aus dem ganzen Ring einen Spazierpark. So nutzen ihn die Leute bis heute.
localizedExtendedStory.en: Lucca's wall runs 4 kilometres and 223 metres around the town, with eleven bastions set into it. This is one of them, and an older tower sits swallowed up inside its bulk. Galleries run underneath it. In 2024 they opened as a permanent exhibition about the wall, entered from via delle Conce. In the 1820s Maria Luisa of Bourbon turned the whole circuit into a walking park. That is what people use it for now.

localizedStory.de: Eine von elf Bastionen auf einer Mauer, die heute Park ist. In ihr steckt ein älterer Turm.
localizedStory.en: One of eleven bastions on a wall that is now a park. An older tower is buried inside this one.

fruits.name: Baluardo Santa Croce
fruits.story: One of eleven bastions on a wall that is now a park. An older tower is buried inside this one.

fruits.extendedStory: The church dates from 1430 and carries the name of Francis of Assisi. Its walls follow the Romanesque manner, the building style of round arches. It sits away from the busiest streets, and the quiet around it is part of what you notice when you arrive. The name has been on it for close to six centuries.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Die Kirche stammt von 1430 und trägt den Namen des Franz von Assisi. Ihre Mauern folgen der romanischen Bauweise, dem Stil der Rundbögen. Sie liegt abseits der belebtesten Gassen, und die Ruhe ringsum gehört zu dem, was man beim Ankommen bemerkt. Der Name steht seit bald sechs Jahrhunderten an ihr.
localizedExtendedStory.en: The church dates from 1430 and carries the name of Francis of Assisi. Its walls follow the Romanesque manner, the building style of round arches. It sits away from the busiest streets, and the quiet around it is part of what you notice when you arrive. The name has been on it for close to six centuries.

localizedStory.de: Diese Kirche von 1430 trägt den Namen des Franz von Assisi.
localizedStory.en: This church of 1430 carries the name of Francis of Assisi.

fruits.name: Chiesa di San Francesco
fruits.story: This church of 1430 carries the name of Francis of Assisi.

fruits.extendedStory: Elisa Bonaparte Baciocchi ruled Lucca as princess, and in 1806 she wanted her palace given room to be seen. Houses, shops, warehouses, a tower, an archive and the church of San Pietro Maggiore all came down for it. Maria Luisa of Bourbon later swapped the elms for plane trees. Her statue stands here with her son Carlo Lodovico, carved by Lorenzo Bartolini.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Elisa Bonaparte Baciocchi regierte Lucca als Fürstin und wollte 1806 ihrem Palast Platz zum Gesehenwerden verschaffen. Häuser, Läden, Lager, ein Turm, ein Archiv und die Kirche San Pietro Maggiore fielen dafür. Maria Luisa von Bourbon tauschte später die Ulmen gegen Platanen. Ihr Standbild steht hier mit ihrem Sohn Carlo Lodovico, gehauen von Lorenzo Bartolini.
localizedExtendedStory.en: Elisa Bonaparte Baciocchi ruled Lucca as princess, and in 1806 she wanted her palace given room to be seen. Houses, shops, warehouses, a tower, an archive and the church of San Pietro Maggiore all came down for it. Maria Luisa of Bourbon later swapped the elms for plane trees. Her statue stands here with her son Carlo Lodovico, carved by Lorenzo Bartolini.

localizedStory.de: Napoleons Schwester ließ diesen Platz 1806 anlegen. Eine ganze Kirche musste dafür weichen.
localizedStory.en: Napoleon's sister opened this square in 1806. A whole church had to come down to make room.

fruits.name: Piazza Napoleone
fruits.story: Napoleon's sister opened this square in 1806. A whole church had to come down to make room.
